title: Türkiye's Central Bank Holds Rates at 37% as Oil Above $100 Threatens Disinflation; Erdoğan Meets Ankara Mayor Yavaş Amid Opposition Realignment
subhead: The CBRT kept its policy rate on hold for a fifth straight meeting, citing fresh US-Iran fighting pushing Brent above $100 and complicating Türkiye's disinflation drive, while a surprise closed-door Erdoğan-Yavaş meeting fueled speculation about the opposition's trajectory.

sections.heading: Central Bank Holds Rates at 37% as Oil Prices Cloud Disinflation Path
sections.body:
The Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) kept its one-week repo rate at 37% on Thursday for a fifth consecutive meeting, in line with market expectations, per Türkiye Today. The bank's statement took a more confident tone than in July, saying 'recent inflation figures and leading indicators suggest that the underlying trend of inflation is decelerating.' However, it warned that 'elevated energy prices amid geopolitical developments pose an upward risk to the inflation outlook' as renewed US-Iran fighting pushed Brent crude above $100 a barrel.

August inflation slowed to 31.5% year-on-year with monthly price change holding at 1.8%, though energy costs rose 5.5% month-over-month. Türkiye Today reports the bank recently returned to funding the market through regular one-week repo auctions in late August after suspending them on March 1, effectively lowering market funding costs by about 300 basis points. Gasoline is up 14.4% and diesel up 9.7% versus a month earlier, even as the government restored a diesel special consumption tax to ₺3 per liter on Sept. 1, set to rise ₺3 each month through December.

Analysts see a split path: Alnus Investment believes the CBRT's emphasis on slowing underlying inflation could leave room for two rate cuts by year-end, while Tacirler Investment says the bank will likely wait, noting Brent above $100 and renewed geopolitical tensions require monitoring external developments for more time. The next policy meeting is Oct. 22, followed by Dec. 10.
sections.whyItMatters: The hold confirms Türkiye's disinflation program is hostage to the regional oil shock — the bank is now weighing the pass-through from fuel prices against evidence of weak domestic demand, with the effective easing from the repo-auction restart already doing some of the CBRT's work for it.

sections.heading: Erdoğan Meets Ankara Mayor Yavaş, Fueling Opposition Realignment Speculation
sections.body:
A closed-door meeting between President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Ankara Mayor Mansur Yavaş at the Presidential Complex on Sept. 9 — their first one-on-one since 2020 — has triggered a political stir, according to Hürriyet Daily News and Türkiye Today. Yavaş, widely seen as a prospective 2028 presidential candidate, said the talks covered only Ankara's metro investments, municipal financing, and a planned fair and congress center, and he repeatedly denied intentions to leave the CHP or join the AK Party.

The encounter comes amid a major opposition reshuffle: Özgür Özel and 90 other lawmakers resigned from the CHP on July 24 to found the Yeni Party after a court ruling removed Özel from the CHP leadership, making it Parliament's second-largest bloc. Several CHP-elected mayors have since moved to the new party. Yavaş said he informed both Özel and CHP leader Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu in advance of the meeting; Özel confirmed Yavaş sought the appointment over Ankara investments, saying 'We have no doubt about him.'

The presidency confirmed the meeting but gave no details. Yavaş also thanked Erdoğan for Ankara hosting the NATO Summit, according to Türkiye Today.
sections.whyItMatters: The meeting signals how fluid Türkiye's opposition is: a potential presidential contender is now in direct, cordial contact with Erdoğan while formally still aligned with the opposition, a dynamic that reshapes the arithmetic of both the ruling bloc and the divided opposition ahead of 2028.

sections.heading: Israel Names New Envoy to Türkiye as Herzog Courts Cyprus
sections.body:
Israel's new top diplomatic envoy to Türkiye, Joel Lion, presented his credentials to the Turkish Foreign Ministry in Ankara on Wednesday, taking up the post of acting chargé d'affaires as bilateral ties remain strained, per The Algemeiner and the Times of Israel. Lion, a former ambassador to Ukraine, Moldova, and Armenia, replaces Irit Lillian, who retired over the summer. He is expected to work primarily from Israel, as the Israeli embassy in Türkiye remains closed and Ankara has recalled its own ambassador.

In a parallel regional move, Israeli President Isaac Herzog arrived in Cyprus on Thursday for his third visit since taking office, meeting President Nikos Christodoulides and voicing hope for a trilateral meeting that would include Lebanon, per Philenews and Yahoo News. The visit carries weight as Israel deepens security ties with Greece and Cyprus — including a reported $3.5 billion Israel-Greece air defense deal — while Turkish-Israeli rivalry extends from Syria into the eastern Mediterranean.

The Algemeiner notes Israeli media have reported scenarios in which a potential confrontation with Türkiye could involve strikes on Turkish military targets in northern Cyprus if Jerusalem deemed Ankara's presence there a threat.
sections.whyItMatters: Türkiye is being squeezed on two fronts of the same axis: Israel keeps a functioning diplomatic channel while simultaneously deepening military ties with Greece and Cyprus, meaning Ankara's Aegean dispute is now embedded in a broader Israel-aligned security realignment.

sections.heading: Iraq Finalizes Air-Defense Deals with US, South Korea, Türkiye
sections.body:
Iraq has finalized contracts for new air defense systems from the United States, South Korea, and Türkiye, with first deliveries due shortly as Baghdad prepares to regain control of its airspace when the US-led coalition mission in Iraq expires on Sept. 30, reports IraqiNews. The systems include South Korea's M-SAM 2, part of a plan to build an integrated long-, medium-, and short-range network backed by radar and command systems protecting oil installations and critical infrastructure.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has compressed Iraq's air-defense modernization timeline from six years to three, a direct response to Iraq's airspace becoming a corridor for missiles, drones, and aircraft during the regional war involving Iran, the US, and Israel, per IraqiNews. Iran has directly struck US sites in Iraq, exposing Baghdad's limited independent capacity to defend its skies. The new systems arrive as Operation Inherent Resolve officially ends inside Iraq at month's end.
sections.whyItMatters: Türkiye gains a fresh export foothold in Iraq's air-defense modernization as the coalition departs — a strategic opening in a market Ankara has long sought, and one that extends its defense-industrial presence into a theater where it also runs cross-border operations.

sections.heading: Türkiye, Italy Sign Cooperation Deal on Labor and Social Policy
sections.body:
Türkiye and Italy signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation in labor and social policies on Sept. 10, according to Daily Sabah and Anadolu Agency. The deal was formalized between the Turkish and Italian labor ministries, with Anadolu reporting the pact aims to deepen coordination on workforce, employment, and social policy issues between the two countries.

Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani has in recent years sought to deepen Ankara-Rome ties as a European interlocutor for Türkiye, and the labor accord adds a functional layer to that relationship.
sections.whyItMatters: A low-key but telling signal of Türkiye maintaining constructive bilateral channels with a key EU member even as the broader EU-Türkiye relationship remains stalled on enlargement and other dossiers.

sections.heading: Greek PM's Megisti Visit Keeps Aegean Wrinkle in View
sections.body:
Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is set to spend his weekend on the island of Megisti, roughly one nautical mile from the Turkish coast, in a move Daily Sabah characterized as Athens signaling its Aegean posture at a moment of elevated tension. The visit comes as the Greek-Israeli military partnership grows and Türkiye's disputes with both countries sharpen.

The symbolic proximity of Megisti to the Turkish mainland is a recurring irritant in Ankara-Athens relations, resurfacing in coverage as Türkiye watches the Greece-Israel defense deepening with concern, per The Algemeiner.
sections.whyItMatters: The Aegean dispute remains a live, low-boil irritant, now compounded by Israel's growing stake in Greece's military posture — a combination Ankara sees as transforming a bilateral disagreement into a wider regional alignment.

bottomLine: Today's dominant Turkish story is economic: the central bank held rates at 37% for a fifth straight meeting as oil above $100 — driven by renewed US-Iran fighting — threatens the disinflation drive, with analysts split on whether cuts can still come by year-end. Politically, a surprise Erdoğan-Yavaş meeting underscored the fluidity of an opposition mid-realignment, while Türkiye's regional environment tightened on the Israel-Cyprus-Greece axis and gained a new defense-export opening in Iraq. The day's thread: Türkiye is managing multiple fronts — inflation at home, a reshuffled opposition, a strained but functional channel to Israel, and expanding defense ties in Iraq — even as the energy shock remains the single biggest variable in its economic outlook.
sources: Türkiye Today, Hürriyet Daily News, Daily Sabah, Anadolu Agency, The Algemeiner, Times of Israel, Philenews, Yahoo News, IraqiNews, Reuters
